articleTitle: Family of generalized Demidenko functionals for robust estimation
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: Problem of filtering of piecewise constant signal corrupted by additive Gaussian or Laplacian noise is considered. Efficiency of minimum duration functionals based on Demidenko function is analyzed. It is shown, that myriad and meridian functionals are the limit forms of generalized Demidenko ones.

articleTitle: Validation of loop-star basis function approach to model EM/EMI problems on complicated surface and wire geometries from low to microwave frequencies
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: In this work, loop-star basis function approach is applied to overcome low frequency breakdown problem for multiple, complicated and mixed surface and wire geometries placed in free space, over ground plane or over/in layered medium. Specifically, it is extended to considering printed structures from low to microwave frequencies. The developed approach is validated on semi-analytical and measurement data for various practical EM/EMI problems.

articleTitle: Sound radiation from roadway with a right-angle winding
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: The sound generation from vehicles moving on the right-angle bend on city road with taking into account of wind effect in the acoustic field is considered. A solution of the problem is found using the integral Fourier transforms, stationary phase method and superposition of many partial solutions. The numerical analysis of traffic noise characteristics is carried out for the case of dual-carriageway Zjednoczenia street in the town of Zielona Góra, Poland.

articleTitle: Antenna synthesis with flat radiating aperture according to the prescribed directivity pattern by power
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: The investigations of solutions of antenna synthesis problem with flat radiating aperture according to the prescribed requirements to the directivity pattern (DP) by power dependent on two physical parameters describing the electrical and physical sizes of aperture and solid angle, in which the necessary DP is given, are presented. It is shown that the non-uniqueness and bifurcation of solutions is characteristic features of this class of problems. The equation on finding such set of values of parameters at which bifurcation of solutions occurs, is found. Numerical algorithms for finding the optimal solutions of the synthesis problem are constructed. The numerical examples are given.

articleTitle: Synthesis of plane equidistant array according to power radiation pattern
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: The variational approach for investigation of solution to nonlinear synthesis problem of plane rectangular equidistant array is used. The functional representing the mean-square deviation of the given and received power radiation patterns including the term with norm of currents is minimized. The nonlinear equation is obtained and the bifurcation of its solutions is studied numerically.

articleTitle: Sound radiation from airplane on the start
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: The problem of sound radiation from airplane during start on runway of aerodrome in wind action conditions is considered. The carriers of sound are aircraft engines, which are modeling in this paper by point sources moving in air with constant acceleration parallel to the plane interface of acoustic and solid elastic half-spaces. The solution of problem is obtained using the integral Fourier-transforms over time and space coordinates, and the stationary phase method. The numerical analysis of spatial-time distributions of instantaneous sound pressure and sound pressure level is carried out for a case of start of the two-engine airplane of Boeing 777-300ER type.

articleTitle: Convergence of electromagnetic model of E-cross for six-port reflectometer
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: The problem of creating meter of complex reflection coefficient based on the electromagnetic approach using E-plane cross-shaped splitter at the measurement transducer is studied. System of the integral equation describing scattering waves by the E-cross is solved. Intrinsic convergence of numeric algorithm is investigated in conventional and modified forms. Procedure of improving of numeric convergence is proposed. Influence of accuracy of electromagnetic model on errors of magnitude of reflection of vibrating load is demonstrated.

articleTitle: About numerical solution of some integral equations of the first kind. — I. optimal approximations
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: Modeling of electrostatic fields at the environments with different characters lead to necessity of solution of the various boundary value problems for the Laplacian in R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> in the case of closed and tired boundary surfaces. Integral equations method allows to avoid the direct solving or significantly to simplify such process for the series of boundary value problems for the Laplacian [1]. The bilateral Dirichlet problem at the Hilbert space the normal derivative elements of which has the jump through boundary surface or the Neumann problem at the Hilbert space the elements of which has the jump through boundary surface such problems includes. Solution of these problems we obtain by means of the simple and double layer potentials by substituting instead of corresponding potential densities the values of difference of the boundary conditions. Solution of bilateral Dirichlet and Neumann problems at the Hilbert space elements of which as their normal derivatives has the jump through boundary surface by means of the sum of simple and double layer potentials reduce to solving only one integral equation of the first kind for simple layer potential in the case of Dirichlet problem and integral equation of the first kind for double layer potential in the case of Neumann problem [1].

articleTitle: Wideband field compensation
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: The compensation method permitting to reduce irradiation of the user's body and to create a weak field area (a dark spot) in the antenna near region for an operation in a wide frequency band is considered.

articleTitle: On the convergence velocity of the modified method of successive approximations in generalized spectral problems
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: The modified method of successive approximations [1-3] is used to calculate characteristic numbers and corresponding eigenfunctions of a given linear completely continuous operator acting in a normalized space. While the operator acts in a Gilbert space, the method converges as a geometrical progression with any small denominator [4]. The method was expanded on spectrum problems with polynomial operator pencils in [5, 6]. In this article it is shown that the convergence velocity of a operator pencil eigenvalues calculated by the method has the same properties as in a linear case.

articleTitle: Interaction of normally incident plane electromagnetic wave with strained dielectric layer
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: Reflection of normally incident polarized electromagnetic wave by a strained dielectric layer, transmission of the wave through the layer and changing its polarization state is considered in the paper. Possibilities of application of the obtained results for non-destructive determination of strain-stressed state of dielectric solids with use of electromagnetic methods are discussed.

articleTitle: Steady-state acoustic scattering by cracked oil pipeline
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: The exact solution of problem for plane stationary sound wave scattering from a cylindrical shell weakened by long linear slit is found. The shell is submerged in ideal fluid and filled by a viscous fluid. The vibration of elastic thin shell is described by the Kirchhoff-Love theory. The numerical analysis of form-function versus the dimensionless frequency or slit location is carried out. The influence of shell geometrical defect on diffraction process is studied.

articleTitle: Asymptotic solution for Bragg couplings of wave beam and two surface waves on nonperiodically inhomogeneous impedance rod
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: A rod with nonperiodically oscillated perturbation of surface impedance is considered. The Krylov-Bogoliubov-Mitropolsky asymptotic method is used for solving boundary-value problem describing electromagnetic wave propagation in the open waveguiding structure. Mutual transformations of a wave beam falling onto inhomogeneous impedance rod and two surface waves propagating along this rod are investigated. Analytical solutions for some particular cases are obtained.

articleTitle: Some properties of the zeros of Kummer function and their application in the analysis of the circular waveguide completely filled with azimuthally magnetized ferrite
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: The Kummer function method is one of the most promising tools for investigation of normal and slow TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0n</inf> modes in the circular waveguides, loaded with co-axially positioned azimuthally magnetized ferrite cylinder [1]. Compared to other approaches, elaborated for the purpose [2–5], its main advantage consists in the very well developed theory of the function mentioned [6] which facilitates the solution of propagation problems and in the possibility to obtain exact results. Competitive to it are the technique, using the Whittaker first function [7] and the quite recently suggested one, employing the regular Coulomb wave function [8].

articleTitle: Study of antenna matching influence on the results of RF exposure simulations
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: The goal of this paper is to explain some inconsistent results obtained during EM exposure numerical simulations and measurements of temperature rise and SAR. After completing the research in terms of MMF II project [1, 2] it became obvious that the understanding of this problem is not complete, and we have to consider some additional aspects. One of them is the presence of a hand, which is discussed in literature [2]. The other parameter is the antenna matching.

articleTitle: Interaction of SH-polarization ultrasonic beam with strained elastic layer
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: In frame of the model for elastic disturbance propagation in in-homogeneously strained elastic continuum, with use the approximation of geometric optics, the interaction of ultrasonic beam of SH-polarization with strained elastic layer is considered. The influence of plane strain parameters on the parameters of reflected and refracted waves in the system "elastic half-space - the layer - elastic half-space" is studied.

articleTitle: The Electromagnetic properties of the finite periodic lattice with “Cassini” elements, embedded in the usual dielectric
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: The electromagnetic (EM) field's diffraction problem on the finite periodic lattice embedded in the usual dielectric is considered. The element of the lattice represents the conductor wire with small electrical radius and with shape of the Cassini oval. Such structures have interesting resonant properties in wide frequency range. The Method of Auxiliary Sources (MAS) is used to solve this problem. The first part of this paper represents the theoretical background for considered problem. Next are presented some numerical results which we obtained using the computer simulation.

articleTitle: SH-waves interaction with finite crack in an elastic layer
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: In this paper we have analyzed the SH elastic wave diffraction by the finite crack located in an elastic layer. The Wiener-Hopf technique is applied to reduce the problem to the infinite system of linear algebraic equations. The wave modes transformation at the crack's tip properties and spectral characteristics of the dynamic problem are investigated.

articleTitle: The excitation of a nonlinear layered medium by a packet of plane waves at multiple frequencies
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: Nonlinear dielectrics with controllable permittivity are subject of intense studies and begin to find broad applications in device technology and electronics. We develop a model of resonance scattering and generation of waves on an isotropic nonmagnetic nonlinear layered dielectric structure excited by a packet of plane waves in the resonance frequency range in a self-consistent formulation. Various effects caused by the nonlinearity of the structure are investigated using analytical and numerical techniques.

articleTitle: Penetration of a plain electromagnetic wave into multilayer dielectric with periodic grating
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: Penetration of a plane electromagnetic wave through a multilayer dielectric Radome, containing a periodic grating, formed of perfectly conducting cylinders of a circular cross-section is considered. It is shown that in Wood's anomaly modes the grating does not affect on the normal functionality and in particular conditions it is completely transparent.

articleTitle: Scattering of H-polarized electromagnetic wave by dielectric covered slotted cylinder co-axially coupled with metal cylinder sector
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: Scattering of electromagnetic wave is considered for a composite cylindrical structure consisting of a dielectric covered slotted cylinder co-axially coupled with a metal cylinder sector. The boundary-value method is employed using completeness property of the angular functions in the respective intervals. Problem is reduced to solution of system of algebraic equations of second kind for the unknown coefficients of Fourier expansion of scattered field. Analytical solution is obtained for certain value of cylinder slot-width. Scattered far-field and back radar cross section (BRCS) of the structure are formulated.

articleTitle: Technology for production of carbon nanoparticles doped with magnetic clusters
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: The original ethanol pyrolysis and chemical vapor deposition data speak on production of randomly distributed carbon nanoparticles aggregations doped with iron magnetic nanoclusters of 150 nm mean size. The data are supported by the results of magnetometry measurements.

articleTitle: Use of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) vs. acoustic imaging to assess the severity of Mitral Regurgitation
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: Precise estimation of the amount of blood that leaks from the left ventricle to the left atrium is necessary to assess the severity of the Mitral Regurgitation (MR). While the present gold standard to asses MR is by echocardiography, in this work we propose a new approach to estimating MR using velocity values measured with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The volume estimation is based on the velocity of the blood through a number of slices. In contrast to echocardiography which is based on acoustic waves, the proposed algorithm is not based on any assumption concerning the shape of the orifice through which blood flows. The proposed algorithm has been tested on MRI scans from patients with moderate-severe MR and compared to acoustic imaging results, providing results that are robust to parameters selection however underestimate the size of the leak. Our conclusion is that adjusted MRI could be an efficient robust tool to assess the severity of Mitral Regurgitation instead of acoustic imaging.

articleTitle: About scattered field's singularities and Rayleigh hypothesis
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: The new vision on the Rayleigh hypothesis is discussed based on several new results of computer simulations. Possible or actual singularities in the analytic continuation of the scattering problem solutions for the two and tree dimensional Helmholtz equation are studied in order to investigate the Rayleigh hypothesis validity. The procedure uses computer simulations for the solution particular problems, and relates to the several types of singularities, associated with the elementary source as well as boundary curve's singularities in the solution. The results provide confirmation of criteria for the validity of the Rayleigh hypothesis that have been criticized by several investigators, including us. In this paper it is demonstrated, that the Rayleigh hypothesis might be correct and has deep physical meaning.

articleTitle: ONVMS applied to a new advanced portable EMI system data
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: The ortho-normalized volume magnetic source (ONVMS) technique is applied to a new time domain EMI instrument called portable decoupled electromagnetic induction sensor (PEDEMIS); The system provides multiple deployment options (carted or carried); multimode operation (detection, interrogation, deep detection, wide interrogation); multi static data that is collected with flexible, decoupled and detachable sensors with precise positioning. In this paper we first describe the geometries of the PEDEMIS transmitters and receivers, then present the procedures to model the way they establish primary fields and measure subsurface responses, and, finally, illustrate the comparisons between modeled and actual data.

articleTitle: Apodized quasiperiodic Bragg structures with thin contrast layers
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: Simply realized constructions of periodic and quasiperiodic structures of apodized Bragg reflectors and resonators with thin contrast layers have been proposed. The results of numerical simulation and measurements for such structures have been obtained.

articleTitle: Reliability indices of composite electromagnetic systems
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: Models for main reliability indices of composite electromagnetic systems are examined in this paper. A method of investigation of reliability indices for composite systems by means of generating systems is developed taking account of aging of systems' output elements. Expressions for the probability distribution calculation of count of operating output elements, the availability function, the failure probability, the failure frequency and the failure rate are worked out in the cases when the lifetime of ageing output elements is circumscribed by the Weibull distribution.

articleTitle: Wideband compensation with flat reflectors
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: Compensation structures with one and two flat reflectors are suggested and analyzed.

articleTitle: The MAS based simulation of plane wave angular incident on two-dimensional dielectric sphere array
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: In this article, the Method of Auxiliary Sources (MAS) is applied for analysis of angular incident of electromagnetic plane wave on two-dimensional dielectric sphere arrays. Homogeneous dielectrics spheres are placed on rectangular grid. To fulfill the Floquet conditions, in the MAS algorithm the lattice sum of electric dipoles is applied as a Green's function. The structures are investigated numerically. The MAS approach is applied to periodic structures. The presented results demonstrate the arrays as Frequency Selective Surfaces (FSS).

articleTitle: Solution of large-scale underwater acoustic problems using fast boundary element method
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: This paper develops the fast multipole method (FMM) accelerated the boundary element method (BEM) for large-scale underwater acoustic problems. The Burton-Miller formulation is employed to overcome non-uniqueness difficulties in the conventional BEM for exterior acoustic problems. The computational efficiency is further improved by adopting the FMM to solve system matrix equation. Numerical results clearly demonstrate the complete reliability and efficiency of the FMM-BEM algorithm.

articleTitle: Novel compact spider microstrip antenna with new Defected Ground Structure
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: Two novel Defected Ground Structures (DGS) were first proposed, which have better results than that of the dumbbell (published shape). Using the general model of DGS, its equivalent parameters were extracted. The two new proposed shapes of DGS were then used to design a novel compact spider microstrip antenna to minimize its area. The size of the developed antenna was reduced to about 90.5% of that of the conventional one. This antenna with two different novel shapes of DGS was designed and simulated by using the ready-made software package Zeland-IE3D. Finally, it was fabricated by using thin film and photolithographic technique and measured by using vector network analyzer. Good agreements were found between the simulated and measured results.

articleTitle: Application of acoustic wave scattering on the small particles for the non-destructive testing
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: The theory of scattering of the acoustic waves on the small bodies is applied to solution of problem related to the non-destructive testing of materials with defects. The change of the refraction coefficient of the acoustic wave passing through the steel pattern testifies to presence of microdefects in material. The numerical results are presented for several kinds of steel and they confirm the possibility to apply the asymptotic scattering theory to problems of the non-destructive testing.

articleTitle: The influence of the probe on the circular aperture near field
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: The axial symmetric TM-wave diffraction by the circular aperture with the presence of conical probe is analyzed rigorously using the mode-matching and analytical regularization techniques. The problem is reduced to the solution of infinite system of linear algebraic equations of the second kind. The numerical examples of the near field characteristics are discussed. The effect of the near field penetrating through the small hole is analyzed.

articleTitle: Scattering of SH-waves by a thin piezoelectric inclusion of low rigidity
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: The antiplane dynamic problem for an elastic medium with a thin linear piezoelectric inclusion of low rigidity is considered. The methodology of investigation is based on the method of matched asymptotic expansions and the integral equations method. Wave fields scattered by the inclusion into the far zone (Fraunhofer zone) are investigated.

articleTitle: Propagation of transverse — Magnetic wave in a waveguide with an anisotropic magnetodielectric plate of finite thickness
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: The reflection and transition of transverse - magnetic (TM) wave from the anisotropic magnetodielectric plate in the waveguide of arbitrary cross section is considered. The power reflection and transmission coefficients for the plate are obtained. The analysis of dependence of these coefficients on thickness of the plate in the waveguide is lead.

articleTitle: Long-term memory and magnetoacoustic responses at excitation of magnetostrictive materials by RF pulses using pulsed NMR technique
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: Different long-term acoustic memory and magnetoacoustic effects were observed in magnetostrictive materials at their inductive excitation by radiofrequency (RF) pulses using pulsed NMR techniques. Along it the stimulated domain-acoustic echo, possessing a long-term acoustic memory was inductively excited by three RF pulses in magnetite and magnetoelectric ferrite-piezoelectric layered composites using pulsed NMR technique with inductive and electric recording of DAE signals.

articleTitle: Radar protection of impedance sphere and other nonplanar surfaces
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: It is known that the sphere is invisible for the radar if its surface has the unit impedance, similarly as the plane does not reflect the normally falling plane wave. Here the question is investigated which concerns the existence of other impedances which have the same property. Two other values of the complex impedance are obtained, which provide the radar invisibility of the sphere. These values have negative real parts, that is, the surface having such impedance is analogous to an active medium. Numerical results describing the frequency dependences of these impedances are presented. For nonplanar surfaces of complicated shapes the relation between the impedance tensor elements is found which provide the protection, at least, for two orthogonal polarizations of the incident plane wave.

articleTitle: Observation of VLF electromagenetic waves in Tbilisi State University Ionosphere Observatory
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: This article provides insight about signal amplitude variations of VLF band by observing 15 communications radio stations at the same time. The issues addressed include analysis of ionosphere parameters gathered for different geographical regions. Experimental system for multi-frequency observing is presented. The article especially reflects ongoing research within Tbilisi State University Ionosphere Observatory.

articleTitle: Application of the ONVMS model to discriminate challenging UXO targets
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: Discrimination of challenging targets, such as small and deep targets in highly cluttered environments, is still an enormous problem for UXO industry. One way to improve target classification is to enhance the sensor hardware, while another way is to fully utilize the data provided by current EMI sensors, by deploying advanced signal processing approaches. To address the latter, our group developed a new ortho-normalized volume magnetic source (ONVMS) technique for representing subsurface targets responses, and for discriminating between UXO and non-UXO targets. The technique has been applied to live-site UXO data sets and demonstrated to be robust and tolerant to noise. In this paper the ONVMS is applied to the data from a small 20 mm projectile, acquired using an advanced, commercially available EMI system “MetalMapper” (MM). The target intrinsic parameters are first extracted from the data using both the ONVMS and simple dipole models, and then analyzed from library matching classification perspective.

articleTitle: Investigation of achievable accuracy limit of dielectric layer parameters estimates obtained on basis of reflection coefficient measurements
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: Minimum, mean and maximum value of the least achievable variance of dielectric layer parameters estimates are evaluated for typical microwave frequency bands used in practice of nondestructive testing. The values of variance are calculated as Cramér-Rao bounds depending on permittivity and thickness of dielectric layer and parameters of frequency grid. The bounds are compared with result of statistical numeric experiment carried out for the purpose of estimation of permittivity and thickness estimates variance provided by quasisolution method.

articleTitle: About numerical solution of some integral equations of the first kind. — II. projection methods
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: Optimal approximations of the Hilbert spaces where determined the operators of integral equations of the first kind equivalent to bilateral Dirichlet and Neumann problems for the Laplacian in R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> for tired boundary surface were construct in [1]. In this article the projection methods for solving of these equations are investigated.

articleTitle: Modeling of IR-radiation and temperature field in a plane layer
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: An analytical solution for 1-D stationary problem of heat and IRradiation transfer in a plane layer under conductive, convective and radiation energy exchange with the environment has been obtained within the P1-approximation. Problems for heat and IR-radiation transfer in physical objects under their conductive, convective and radiative heat exchange with environment arise, in particular, when methods for non-contact thermometry for metal melts are developed. The paper objective is to study the correlation between the melt temperature and IRradiation emitting by it.

articleTitle: Mutual transformation of vanishing and nonvanishing solutions of a class of nonlinear Hammerstein integral equations
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: A class of nonlinear integral equations of the Hammerstein type connected with the phase optimization problem (antenna synthesis, energy transmitting lines optimization etc.), which have analytical solutions, is considered. The paper develops the early obtained results about connection between the sets of solutions, with or without zeros in their definition domains. The process of mutual transformation of different types of results is numerically analyzed, and other types of branching are investigated.

articleTitle: System of impedance vibrators in free space
publicationTitle: 2012 XVIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory - (DIPED)
abstract: A problem of electromagnetic waves excitation by a system of impedance vibrators in free space is solved by a generalized method of induced electromotive forces (EMF). As an example characteristics of three-element Yagi-Uda antenna for various vibrator lengths and types of the distributed impedance are given.
